content: Reading the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected:** Leaves (two leaves shown — one adaxial/top surface, one abaxial/bottom surface)
- **Lesion characteristics:**
  - Circular to oval necrotic spots on the leaf surface
  - Center of lesions: grayish-white to tan/silvery, sunken appearance
  - Dark brown to black border ring surrounding the necrotic center
  - Yellowish halo visible around at least one lesion (chlorotic halo)
  - Multiple lesions of varying size on the right leaf
- **Pattern:** Discrete, well-defined spots scattered across the leaf blade — classic "eye-spot" appearance with a light center, dark brown ring border, and yellow halo

These symptoms — circular spots with light/tan necrotic centers, dark brown concentric rings, and chlorotic halos — are the hallmark of **Brown Eye Spot** disease, caused by *Cercospora coffeicola* (in coffee) or similar fungal pathogens depending on host. The concentric ring giving the lesion an "eye-like" appearance is the definitive diagnostic feature visible here.
